issuer.summary: USDm is issued by Mento Labs, a German company spun out of Celo's core developer in 2022, with a doxxed chief executive and a $10M Series A. The reserve is held on-chain with no off-chain custodian — but the reserve assets are themselves other issuers' stablecoins, so a holder is exposed to three further issuers rather than to Treasuries: roughly 61% to one, 19% to another, and 19% to a bridged wrapper. The legal wrapper is an ordinary German company with no fund structure and no bankruptcy-remoteness, so holders have no direct legal claim on the reserve. See the full report for the reserve composition and the governance surface.
issuer.summary_source: Internal assessment of the issuing entity, its legal wrapper and the reserve's look-through composition. Reserve percentages are the Monad deployment. [verified 2026-08-23]
facts: Issuer is Mento Labs, a German company spun out of Celo's core developer in 2022. Chief executive is doxxed; the company raised a $10M Series A in October 2024.
✅ NO OFF-CHAIN CUSTODIAN. Reserve assets sit in an on-chain reserve contract directly, so the holdings are independently observable rather than attested.

⚠️⚠️ BUT THE RESERVE IS OTHER ISSUERS' STABLECOINS, so USDm's issuer risk is LAYERED rather than direct: roughly 61% of the Monad reserve is exposure to a newer single-manager issuer, ~19% to a tier-one issuer, and ~19% to a bridged wrapper carrying both bridge and issuer risk.
⚠️ The 61% leg is the concentration that matters — it is an issuer with single-manager and single-custodian concentration of its own, so the exposure compounds rather than diversifies.
⚠️ LEGAL WRAPPER IS AN ORDINARY COMPANY. No fund structure, no bankruptcy-remoteness — holders have NO DIRECT LEGAL CLAIM on the reserve assets.

⚠️ A single 4-of-7 Safe owns the token (mint, burn and upgrade), the reserve contract (which it can drain or reconfigure), the pools, the circuit breaker and the oracle adapter. One key set reaches every surface.

⚠️ NOT the same asset as similarly-tickered dollar tokens from other issuers — this is the Celo/Monad deployment, and confusing it with a Treasury-backed namesake would misstate both the backing and the issuer.
